blocks.text: JavaScript Arrow Functions
Arrow Functions allow a shorter syntax for function expressions.

You can skip the function keyword, the return keyword, and the
curly brackets:
const multiply = (a, b) => a * b;
Try it Yourself »

Arrow Functions were introduced in ES6 and are commonly
used in modern JavaScript.
Arrow Function Syntax
An arrow function uses the => symbol.
An arrow function is always written as a function expression.

blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text: This arrow function does the same thing as a regular function expression.
Shorter Syntax
If the function body contains only one statement:
You can remove the word function, the curly brackets and the return keyword.
const multiply = function(a, b) {return a * b}
blocks.caption: Before Arrow

blocks.text: const multiply = (a, b) => a * b;
blocks.caption: With Arrow

blocks.text: const hello = () => "Hello World!";
blocks.caption: With Arrow

blocks.text: const hello = function() {return "Hello World!";}
blocks.caption: Before Arrow

blocks.text: Arrow Functions with One Parameter
If a function has only one parameter, you can omit the parentheses:
const square = (x) => x * x;
blocks.caption: With Parantheses

blocks.text: const square = x => x * x;
blocks.caption: With Parantheses

blocks.text: const hello = (val) => "Hello " + val;
blocks.caption: With Parantheses

blocks.text: const hello = val => "Hello " + val;
blocks.caption: With Parantheses

blocks.text: Arrow Functions Return Value by Default
If the function has only one statement that returns a value:
You can remove the brackets and the return keyword:
const hello = () => "Hello World!";
blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text: This works only if the function has only one statement.
Arrow Function Parameters
If you have parameters, you pass them inside the parentheses:
const hello = (val) => "Hello " + val;
blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text: If you have only one parameter, you can skip the parentheses as well:
const hello = val => "Hello " + val;
blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text: Arrow Functions with No Parameters
If there are no parameters, parentheses are required.
const hello = () => "Hello World!";
blocks.caption: With Arrow Function:

blocks.text:
You can only omit the return keyword and the curly brackets if the function is a single
statement. Because of this, it might be a good habit to always keep them:

blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text: Arrow Functions Are Not Declarations
Arrow functions are always expressions and must be assigned to a variable.
They cannot be used before they are defined.

hello(); // Error

const hello = () => "Hello";
blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text: Arrow functions must be defined before they are used.
Arrow Functions and the this Keyword
Arrow functions do not have their own this value.
They inherit this from the surrounding code.

Common Mistakes

items:
Forgetting Parentheses Rules
Parentheses are required for zero or multiple parameters.

Using Arrow Functions as Methods
Arrow functions do not bind this.

Expecting Hoisting
Arrow functions are not hoisted.
